time_zone: Program calls carry no session cookie, so ApplicationController's around_action :switch_time_zone, if: :current_user (app/controllers/application_controller.rb lines 14-19, with current_user read from the session at lines 45-47) never runs for them. Time.zone stays Rails' default, UTC, because config.time_zone is left commented out (config/application.rb line 37). A date-only start_date or end_date therefore means 00:00:00 UTC on that day.

order: id, tried only when the identifier is all digits
identifier_lookup.rule: One query loads every user matching any of the four, then the first match in this order wins. The identifier 42 finds the user whose id is 42 before a user whose username is 42. A blank identifier finds nobody.
identifier_lookup.my: The literal my resolves to the caller that the request's credential identifies (StatsController#set_user, stats_controller.rb lines 168-177). Without a usable credential it resolves to nobody, and the action answers 404 User not found.
identifier_lookup.trust_factor_differs: trust_factor has its own lookup over slack_uid and username, plus id when the identifier is all digits. It never tries hca_id and has no my (stats_controller.rb lines 128-138). pairtime answers it with Hackatime's unscored blue value for any user that matches (DESIGN 5.10).

auth.how: No credential. Allowed when the user's stats are public, which is the default (users.allow_public_stats_lookup, HC 1.7).
Authorization: Bearer <the user's API key>. It identifies the caller, which my needs, and lets a user read their own private stats. This action reads Bearer only, not Basic and not ?api_key=.
Authorization: Bearer <OAuth access token with the read scope>, with the same effect as an API key.

params.name: username
params.meaning: Resolved as identifier_lookup describes.

params.name: start_date
params.meaning: Parsed with Time.zone.parse, so in UTC for a program call (see time_zone). A value that doesn't parse gives 422 {"error": "Invalid start_date"}.

params.name: end_date
params.meaning: Parsed like start_date. A bare date means the start of that day, so end_date=2026-11-18 stops at 2026-11-18T00:00:00Z. 422 {"error": "Invalid end_date"} when it doesn't parse.

params.name: features
params.meaning: Comma string of summary sections. projects adds data.projects and languages adds data.languages. Other names are accepted and add nothing.

params.name: filter_by_project
params.meaning: Limits every figure to these Hackatime project names. The value goes through .split(","): a comma string splits into names, and an array goes through ActiveSupport's Array#split, which splits only at elements equal to ",". Both forms filter on the same names, except that a name containing a comma survives only the array form, and a project named exactly "," breaks the array form (stardance app/services/hackatime_service.rb lines 123-128).

params.name: filter_by_category
params.meaning: Comma string. Read only on the total_seconds=true path without test_param.

params.name: test_param
params.meaning: Off unless exactly true. When true the total is boundary-aware, only valid timestamps count, and the categories browsing, meeting and communicating are left out, plus ai coding when no_ai_coding=true, compared with LOWER(category). Stardance always sends it.

params.name: no_ai_coding
params.meaning: true leaves out the ai coding category. Stardance sends false, so its hours include ai coding at full weight.

params.name: total_seconds
params.meaning: Return only {"total_seconds": n}.

params.name: boundary_aware
params.meaning: Read only on the total_seconds=true path without test_param, where it switches that total to the boundary-aware sum with the same category exclusions.

params.name: limit
params.meaning: Caps data.projects and data.languages after they are sorted by seconds.

responses.when: total_seconds is anything but true.
total_seconds=true.
The identifier resolves to nobody, or my comes without a usable credential. Body {"error": "User not found"}.
The user turned public stats off and the caller isn't that user. Body {"error": "user has disabled public stats"}.
start_date or end_date doesn't parse.

notes: With test_param=true, WakatimeService truncates both bounds to whole epoch seconds (convert_to_unix_timestamp, wakatime_service.rb lines 275-292). The boundary-aware total then counts every gap that ends at a heartbeat with start <= time <= end, including the gap from the last matching heartbeat before start (heartbeatable.rb lines 286-311). data.projects counts start <= time < end, with no boundary heartbeat (wakatime_service.rb line 22).
Without test_param, total_seconds=true uses the bounds as parsed, start <= time < end, and the plain sum, or the boundary-aware sum when boundary_aware=true (stats_controller.rb lines 71-90).

Per-project seconds come from the grouped path and the test-mode total from the boundary-aware path, so they don't add up to each other. That is why Stardance makes one total_seconds=true call for each set of linked names (stardance app/services/hackatime_service.rb line 149).

The category exclusion is NOT (LOWER(category) IN (...)), which also drops a heartbeat whose category is NULL. Hackatime's ingest fills in a missing category, coding or browsing by type (HC 1.2), so NULL only appears in rows written some other way.
Unknown parameters are ignored, Stardance's _t cache-buster included.

params.meaning: Parsed with Ruby's Time.parse, which reads a string without an offset in the server process's zone. A string it can't parse raises, and the action doesn't rescue that.

params.meaning: Parsed like start_time.
